subject: anatomy
title: Lymphoid organs and blood vessels: high-yield anatomy and histology

steps.tx: The **lymph node** has an outer **cortex** and an inner **medulla**, surrounded by a fibrous capsule. Just beneath the capsule lies the **subcapsular sinus**, which receives afferent lymph. Cortical follicles contain B cells, and germinal centres appear in secondary follicles after antigenic stimulation. The **paracortex**, between follicles and medullary cords, is rich in T cells.
steps.say: The lymph node has an outer cortex and an inner medulla, enclosed by a fibrous capsule. Just beneath the capsule lies the subcapsular sinus, which receives afferent lymph. Cortical follicles contain B cells, and germinal centres appear in secondary follicles after antigenic stimulation. The paracortex, lying between follicles and medullary cords, is rich in T cells.

steps.tx: Lymphocytes enter the node through **high endothelial venules**, specialised postcapillary venules with cuboidal endothelium. These cells express adhesion molecules that let circulating lymphocytes bind and pass into the tissue. In the thymus, **Hassall corpuscles** are concentric whorls of epithelial reticular cells located in the medulla, and their numbers rise with age.

vis.alt: Schematic of a lymph node: afferent lymphatics enter through the capsule into the subcapsular sinus, cortex holds B cell follicles, paracortex holds T cells and high endothelial venules, medulla has cords and sinuses, efferent lymphatic leaves at the hilum.
vis.caption: Lymph flows in through many afferents and out through one efferent at the hilum; T cells sit in the paracortex, B cells in follicles.

steps.tx: The **spleen** has **white pulp**, formed of lymphoid nodules called Malpighian bodies around a central arteriole, and **red pulp**, made of venous sinusoids and the cords of Billroth. The marginal zone between them holds antigen presenting cells. B cells sit in the follicles and the **periarteriolar lymphatic sheath** holds T cells.
steps.say: The spleen has white pulp, formed of lymphoid nodules called Malpighian bodies around a central arteriole, and red pulp, made of venous sinusoids and the cords of Billroth. The marginal zone between them holds antigen presenting cells. B cells sit in the follicles, and the periarteriolar lymphatic sheath holds T cells.

steps.tx: The **thymus** is the primary lymphoid organ for T cell maturation and has no lymphatic follicles. It is largest in early life, reaching about 35 grams at puberty, then atrophies and is replaced by fat. Neonatal thymectomy depletes thymus-dependent paracortical areas of lymph nodes. Tonsils have **crypts** lined by stratified squamous non-keratinised epithelium.

steps.tx: **Elastic arteries**, such as the aorta, have thick walls rich in elastic lamellae that dampen pulsatile flow. **Muscular arteries** have a thick media of smooth muscle that regulates flow. Arteries carry blood away from the heart and, apart from the pulmonary artery, usually carry oxygenated blood. Arteries have no valves, unlike veins.
